newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST- H.K. newspaper headines - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST- H.K. newspaper headines - Oct 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY - Registration for the post of chief executive started yesterday. Among the eight applicants three were unemployed and most could not fill out the forms correctly.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - The police and other government departments would go on a state of alert after a Japanese sect reportedly threatened to place poison gas in the Mass Transit Railway.
-- Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe had left Hong Kong secretly for San Francisco.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - Governor Chris Patten had ordered to a medical board be set up to determine if District Court Judge Brian Caird was healthy enough to carry out his duties.
-- When meeting different political and social groups, chief executive candidate Peter Woo refused to answer questions about how he would handle cases involving Chinese dissidents.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO - State and Communist Party leaders would be present at the opening ceremony of the 80th Canton Fair in Guangzhou.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - The People's Bank of China instructed departments to take effective measures to strengthen control over overseas Chinese financial organisations.
-- Managing director of Cathay Pacific, Rod Eddington, said that Cathay had no plans to invest in overseas airports, but would continue to seek opportunities to invest in China.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD - Beijing might restrict the final number of chief executive candidates to three, believing that the first chief executive should command high respect from all sectors of society.
-- According to the Hong Kong Investment Fund Association, local equity funds were the best performing group of unit trusts in the 12 months to September 30.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - A senior official said that China meeded at least US$20 billion in foreign investment by 2000 to meet energy targets.
-- Sichuan province plans to float its Chengyu Highway on
an overseas exchange to fund construction of two other road projects. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
